title: Prioritized Task Dependency Schedule
prompt:
Implement `schedule_pending_tasks(tasks, completed=()) -> list[str]`. `tasks` is an insertion-ordered mapping from a nonempty task ID to `{'depends_on': iterable_of_task_ids, 'priority': integer}`. A task may run only after all listed dependencies have completed. `completed` contains task IDs already completed before scheduling; they are omitted from the returned plan. A repeated dependency is one logical dependency.

Return every remaining task in the order a single worker should start it. At each step, choose from currently runnable tasks by higher `priority` first, then lexicographically smaller task ID. Dependencies must name tasks in `tasks`, and all task IDs in `completed` must exist. Raise `ValueError` for an unknown dependency, unknown completed ID, or any dependency cycle. Do not mutate the input mapping or its nested collections.

Use an indegree/reverse-edge traversal plus a priority queue. This is a dependency planning exercise only: do not add task payloads, leases, expiration, snapshots, retries, or concurrency.

example.reasoning: Build has the higher priority but cannot become runnable until fetch has completed.
